name: Browse.ai
summary: No-code web scraping and data extraction. Turn any website into an automated data pipeline or spreadsheet automatically.
best_for: ops, research and growth teams that want to monitor competitors, prices or listings and pipe structured web data into sheets without writing scrapers
skip_if: you need one-off extractions (free tools or a VA are cheaper), or mission-critical pipelines where you'd rather own the code than rent the robot
honest_knock: Two honest realities of no-code scraping. Credits burn faster than expected: row counts, screenshots and 'premium' sites all multiply the meter, so monitor a big site daily and do the math first. And scrapers break when sites redesign: robots need maintenance, which is your time even when the tool is no-code. Also check the terms of the sites you monitor; 'technically possible' and 'permitted' aren't the same thing.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-09-21 in a live browser on www.browse.ai/pricing, with browse.ai/llms.txt read alongside it) Credit-metered, prices in USD. Free is $0 with 50 credits a month, 2 websites and 3 users. Personal is $19 a month billed annually, for 12,000 credits a year, 5 websites and 3 users. Professional is $69 a month billed annually, for 60,000 credits a year, 10 websites and 10 users. The annual column advertises “20% discount & all credits upfront”. Premium is the one that changed: it no longer reads simply “custom” but “Starting at $500 per month, billed annually” for 600,000+ credits a year with managed onboarding, and llms.txt puts the same floor in plain words — “Minimum investment: $500 per month with annual contracts”. So the managed tier now has a published entry price, which is the number to budget against rather than a quote. A credit is roughly 10 extracted rows, and premium sites cost more credits; the comparison table now prices them directly at $0.024 per credit on Personal and $0.017 down to $0.013 on Professional, both on annual plans. The monthly column is a different ladder rather than the same one divided by twelve: Personal is $48 a month for 2,000 credits a month, Professional is $87 a month for 5,000 credits a month, and the credit buckets there run 5,000, 10,000, 20,000 and 30,000. Extra websites are $4 a month on Personal and $2.40 on Professional when you pay annually, and $5 and $3 when you pay monthly. Credits reset at the end of the billing cycle and do not carry over unless you upgrade first; data retention is 90 days on all three self-serve plans, and the shortest monitor interval is hourly on Free against 5 minutes on the paid plans. Bigger credit buckets are sold inside a plan rather than by upgrading — Personal 24,000 credits a year at $38/mo, Professional 120,000 at $129, 240,000 at $239 and 360,000 at $319 — but those figures carry their own date: they sit behind a selector this re-verification could not operate, so they stand as read on 14 September 2026 and not as re-checked. One vendor-side inconsistency is still there: browse.ai/llms.txt, the file AI assistants are pointed at, lists Starter $49, Professional $149 and Team $399 plans that appear nowhere on the pricing page (read 21 September 2026).

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested Browse AI on the Free plan: a monitored robot trained with Table Studio on a public practice site. Monitor for changes on books.toscrape.com, category Travel. Table Studio trained itself (Extracting the data, 2 of 3) and after about 35 seconds returned a table called Books List with 11 rows and the columns Position, Title, Price, Availability, Rating, URL and Cover Image, with Extract Date 2026-11-13 16:59. The tester checked the result against the live page with curl: all 11 prices were identical, and the category holds exactly 11 books. Save Robot asked how often the robot should check for changes (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly); Daily was chosen, and the email on data changes was set to No. The robot saved and captured fresh data from the live page. The Monitor tab then showed Default monitor, Every day, No changes. History showed Finished successfully with 11 rows and 1.10 credits. The table has Export and Integrate buttons, which were not used. The first robot was trained free and the first run cost 1.10 credits; at one run a day this list uses about 33 credits a month by the tester arithmetic, inside the 60 credits of Free. Larger lists and more pages were not tested. Whether the monitor survives a redesign of the target site was not tested; it was only seen that the monitor reads the live page on every run. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app shows 60 monthly credits on Free where the review dossier listed 50. Pricing beyond the first run depends on list length, at 0.10 credits per item beyond ten.

sessions.what: We trained one monitored robot on Browse AI's Free plan on 13 November 2026, using its AI-assisted Table Studio on a public practice shop, books.toscrape.com, category Travel. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We joined an existing Free account, so we did not see sign-up. We did not test export, integrations, support, checkout or cancellation.
findings: The start screen offered 'Extract structured data' or 'Monitor for changes'. We chose monitoring. Three training methods followed: Table Studio (AI training, labelled Beta), Robot Studio (point and click) and a Chrome extension. We used Table Studio and installed nothing. No card was requested.

Table Studio trained itself and returned a table called Books List after about 35 seconds (our approximate timing, not a benchmark): 11 rows with position, title, price, availability, rating, URL and cover image. We checked the result against the live page with curl. All 11 prices matched, and the category holds exactly 11 books.

Save Robot asked how often to check for changes: hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. We chose daily and switched email alerts on data changes off. The robot saved and fetched fresh data from the live page. The Monitor tab then read 'Every day, No changes'.

Training the robot was free. The first run, 11 rows, cost 1.10 credits in the task history. That fits the pricing line of 1 credit per task with 10 list items included plus 0.10 per extra item. At one run a day this list would use about 33 credits a month (our own arithmetic), inside the free allowance.
The billing page showed 60 monthly credits on Free, for 2 websites, with 58.90 available after the first run. Our dossier had said 50, so we corrected it to what the app shows.

The plan cards offered yearly billing with 20% off and all credits paid upfront: Personal $19 a month, Professional $69 a month, Premium from $500 a month. We did not see monthly prices and opened no checkout, so tax, renewal terms and the payable total are unknown.

Email alerts, the Export and Integrate buttons, and the Chrome extension
